whatItIs.text: The dried seed of a parsley-family herb, used whole or ground; its warm, earthy aroma anchors spice blends from taco seasoning to garam masala.

historyNote.text: Cumin is native to the Irano-Turanian region and has been traded for millennia: wild seeds have been dredged up from the sunken settlement of Atlit-Yam (early sixth millennium BC), and ancient Egypt used it in cooking and in mummification.

howToChoose.text: Buy whole seeds when you can and grind as needed — ground cumin loses punch within months; either way it should smell strongly, not dusty.

storage.text: Keep in an airtight tin away from heat and light.

useItUp.text: Toast stale-smelling seeds dry in a pan to wake them up, or infuse into oil for dressings and roasts.

substitutions.note: lighter and citrusy rather than earthy; suits the same dishes gently
